title: Monitoring AI Agents in Production: What to Track and Why
author: Jason D.
excerpt: Deploying is the easy part. Keeping agents reliable over time requires monitoring the right signals. Here's our production monitoring playbook.
content:
Deployment is a milestone, not a finish line. The real work begins when your agent starts processing live traffic. Without the right monitoring, you won't know it's degrading until your operations team tells you — and by then, trust is already damaged.

The Monitoring Stack

Every production AI agent needs monitoring across four dimensions:

1. Accuracy Monitoring

Track the agent's accuracy over time using a sample-based review process. Set up automated sampling that flags cases for human review.

# monitoring_config.yaml
accuracy:
  sample_rate: 0.05        # Review 5% of decisions
  alert_threshold: 0.90    # Alert if accuracy drops below 90%
  window: "24h"            # Rolling 24-hour window
  escalation: "ops-team"   # Who gets the alert

2. Latency Monitoring

Track response times at p50, p95, and p99. Sudden latency spikes often indicate upstream issues or model degradation.

3. Drift Detection

Monitor the distribution of inputs over time. If the types of requests change significantly, the agent may be operating outside its training distribution.

4. Cost Tracking

Track cost per request and total daily spend. AI costs can spike unexpectedly when input patterns change or retry logic runs away.

Alert Design

Good alerts are actionable. Each alert should include:

  • What happened (metric, threshold, current value)
  • Why it matters (business impact)
  • What to do (runbook link or next steps)
  • Who to contact (escalation path)

The goal of monitoring isn't to prevent all failures. It's to detect them fast enough that the impact stays small.

Weekly Review Cadence

Beyond automated monitoring, establish a weekly review:

  • Review sampled accuracy results
  • Check for new failure patterns
  • Update evaluation suite with new edge cases
  • Review cost trends
  • Assess whether business KPIs are tracking

The Bottom Line

Monitoring isn't optional. It's the difference between an agent that works today and one that works six months from now. Invest in it early, review it weekly, and treat every failure as a learning opportunity.
